name: NULLFEST — The Abandoned Infrastructure Rave Circuit
creator: Ghost Frequency Network (rotating collective)
description: NULLFEST is a three-day annual rave held in a different decommissioned Shelf infrastructure site each year — past venues have included a drained water treatment reservoir, a collapsed transit interchange, and a seven-story parking structure filled with fog machines and jury-rigged speaker arrays. Location is distributed only through encrypted BCI channels 72 hours before start, and attendance is strictly by word-of-mouth. The music is a continuous collaborative neural-feed mix of Afrobeat-derived percussion, Maghrebi synthesizer traditions, and industrial noise.
medium: physical attendance, pirate neural feed audio, BCI-synced haptic rigs
cultural_impact: NULLFEST is the most famous underground music event in GLMZ, functioning as both hedonistic release valve and organizing ground for Shelf political networks — deals are made, movements are born, and information is exchanged in the noise.
controversy: Corponation security and MMA have raided four NULLFEST events; the 2211 raid resulted in thirty-seven arrests and two deaths, making it a rallying point for Shelf civil rights organizing.
story_hooks: A MMA undercover officer embedded in the NULLFEST planning collective has been attending for two years and has stopped wanting to file reports.
The 2225 NULLFEST venue — a sealed pre-Collapse water vault — contains something that was deliberately hidden there, and the organizers don't know it yet.

A Tier 4 music producer attends NULLFEST using a black-market identity chip and offers the collective a legitimate recording contract — and the collective has to vote on whether to destroy itself or scale up.
